answer: Data-shard custody enforces sybil-resistance by requiring 1,000 units to secure a unique file, acting as a velvet filter against automated bloat. A verifier audits these shards through random retrieval proofs; should an identity wander from its data, the identity is revoked. An honest participant pays 1,000 units, while 1,000 fakes cost 1,000,000. Each node acts as a marble entry in an immutable registry.
